solution.description: Treat 68 as one below 69, a number ending in 9. That converts the whole problem into the auxiliary fraction 1.5 over 7, so every later step divides by 7 instead of by 68.
Begin the expansion by dividing the auxiliary numerator. Seven goes into 15 twice with 1 left over, so the first decimal digit is 2 and the remainder carried forward is 1.

solution.operation: Next dividend = 12 + 2 = 14; Divide 14 by 7: Q=2, R=0
solution.description: Form the next dividend by writing the remainder 1 in front of the digit just produced, giving 12, then add that same quotient digit 2, the correction owed because 68 sits one below 69. Dividing 14 by 7 gives a second digit of 2 with nothing left over.

solution.operation: Next dividend = 02 + 2 = 04; Divide 04 by 7: Q=0, R=4
solution.description: Remainder 0 in front of the new digit 2 gives 02, and adding the previous quotient digit 2 makes 4. Seven does not go into 4, so the third digit is 0 and the whole 4 becomes the remainder.

solution.operation: Next dividend = 40 + 0 = 40; Divide 40 by 7: Q=5, R=5
solution.description: Remainder 4 in front of the digit 0 gives 40, and the previous quotient digit 0 adds nothing. Seven goes into 40 five times with 5 left over, so the fourth digit is 5.

solution.operation: Next dividend = 55 + 5 = 60; Divide 60 by 7: Q=8, R=4
solution.description: Remainder 5 in front of the digit 5 gives 55, and adding the previous quotient digit 5 makes 60. Seven goes into 60 eight times with 4 left over, so the fifth digit is 8.

Repeat the same short loop, remainder in front of the last digit, add that digit, divide by 7, and the digits 2, 2, 0, 5, 8 run on into the full sixteen-place expansion. No division by 68 is ever performed.

examples.problem_statement: Divide 15 by 68 using the conventional long division method.

solution.description: Since 15 is smaller than 68 there is no whole-number part. Place the decimal point in the quotient and append zeros to 15 so the division can proceed.
Divide 150 by 68: two 68s make 136, leaving 14. The first digit after the decimal point is 2, and 14 carries forward as the remainder.
Bring down a zero to turn remainder 14 into 140. Two 68s make 136 again, so the next digit is 2 and the remainder is 4.
Bring down a zero to turn remainder 4 into 40. Because 40 is smaller than 68 the quotient digit is 0, and the whole 40 carries forward.
Bring down another zero, making 400. Five 68s make 340, so the next digit is 5 and the remainder is 60.
Bring down a zero to make 600. Eight 68s make 544, so the next digit is 8 and the remainder is 56.
Bring down a zero to make 560. Eight 68s make 544 once more, giving another 8 with remainder 16.
Bring down a zero to make 160. Two 68s make 136, so the next digit is 2 and the remainder is 24.
Bring down a zero to make 240. Three 68s make 204, so the next digit is 3 and the remainder is 36.
Bring down a zero to make 360. Five 68s make 340, giving the digit 5 and remainder 20. Nine digits in, the quotient reads 0.220588235, and the same subtract-and-bring-down loop keeps going.

138 goes into 1220 eight times (8 × 138 = 1104). Subtract to get remainder 116. Bring down 0 to make 1160.

138 goes into 560 four times (4 × 138 = 552). Subtract to get remainder 8. Bring down 0 to make 80.

138 goes into 1100 seven times (7 × 138 = 966). Subtract to get remainder 134. Bring down 0 to make 1340.
138 goes into 1340 nine times (9 × 138 = 1242). Subtract to get remainder 98. Bring down 0 to make 980.
138 goes into 980 seven times (7 × 138 = 966). Subtract to get remainder 14. Bring down 0 to make 140.
138 goes into 140 once (1 × 138 = 138). Subtract to get remainder 2. Bring down 0 to make 20.
138 goes into 20 zero times. Bring down 0 to make 200.
138 goes into 200 once (1 × 138 = 138). Subtract to get remainder 62. Bring down 0 to make 620.
138 goes into 620 four times (4 × 138 = 552). Subtract to get remainder 68. Bring down 0 to make 680.
138 goes into 680 four times (4 × 138 = 552). Subtract to get remainder 128. Bring down 0 to make 1280.
138 goes into 1280 nine times (9 × 138 = 1242). Subtract to get remainder 38. Bring down 0 to make 380.
